speaker: narrator
text: Act I: The Call to Adventure

speaker: narrator
text: You are Elior, a farmer boy in the village of Willowbrook, on the outskirts of Eldoria. Your grandmother raised you after your parents vanished, and your days are the crops, the hens and the weather.

speaker: narrator
text: Tonight the weather is a storm, and a light that is not lightning has split the sky over the fields. Sleep, when it comes, is not quiet.

speaker: narrator
text: The Dream

speaker: narrator
text: It is dark, and it is raining hard. You hear it beating on shutters, though you cannot see any. Thunder breaks so close that the dark shakes with it. Shadows drift past like smoke. A man’s hand reaches out of the dark, lifts a child and holds it against his shoulder, and then both of them are gone. Somewhere a slow tune climbs three notes and settles home again. A tall figure stands among the shadows. It has no face you can find. It is too far away to reach, and too close to be only a dream. It is whispering, at the very edge of hearing, and what it whispers is your name.

speaker: narrator
text: You answer it. You do not know with what: your own name back, or the question under it.

speaker: narrator
text: The whisper comes once more, closer than the thunder, and this time there are words in it.

speaker: voice
text: …and let them rest… Elior.

speaker: narrator
text: The dark lets go of you, and you wake in your own bed. The storm is gone and there is grey morning in the curtains. Your heart is going hard. The tune is still going too, thin and near: someone is humming it, out by the hearth. Three words are already slipping, and you write them down before they can go.

speaker: narrator
text: It has no face you can find, only a height and a nearness. When it speaks, it speaks your name.

speaker: narrator
text: Your hands find nothing. The dark has no floor and the dream no edges. The whisper comes again, nearer, and it is your name.

speaker: narrator
text: You think it over. Nothing presses on you just now.

speaker: narrator
text: You are asleep already. The voice says your name again, nearer.

speaker: narrator
text: You go that way, and it is the same dark, the same rain, the same tune. There is no door in this. There is only the voice, and it says your name.

speaker: narrator
text: The rain, and the thunder under it. Under the thunder, the tune: three notes climbing, and settling home. You know it, and could not say from where. Under the tune, a whisper, and the whisper is your name.

speaker: narrator
text: Nothing here answers to that. The voice says your name.

speaker: narrator
text: New main quest

speaker: narrator
text: Shadows Over Willowbrook

speaker: narrator
text: Elior dreamed of a storm, a tune, and a figure in the dark that whispered his name. He woke with three words written down: …and let them rest…

speaker: narrator
text: New side quest

speaker: narrator
text: Hint of Magic

speaker: narrator
text: You woke with three words written down and a tune still going in the house. Grandmother is at the hearth, and she will want to hear about the dream.

speaker: narrator
text: You'd rather light the lantern before you carry it anywhere; it is no use to you dark.

speaker: narrator
text: You don't see that here.

speaker: narrator
text: It is quiet here.

speaker: narrator
text: Your grandmother tilts her head.

speaker: grandmother
text: I'm not sure what you mean, dear, but I do like to hear you talk.

speaker: narrator
text: Elior's Cottage

speaker: narrator
text: A modest cottage with a straw roof and a cozy hearth. The scent of fresh bread and old books fills the air. Sunlight filters through lace curtains, illuminating shelves lined with trinkets and memories. A sturdy wooden table sits in the center, and a gentle fire crackles in the hearth. Grandmother stands by it, humming, and keeps an eye on the bread.

speaker: narrator
text: A fire burns low in the stone hearth, and the bricks above it are black from many winters.

speaker: narrator
text: A well-used brass lantern. Its glass is clean and the wick is fresh, ready to light up the darkest corners.

speaker: grandmother
text: There you are. Sit down a minute, the bread's nearly done.

speaker: narrator
text: She does not sit down herself.

speaker: grandmother
text: The village is on edge, you'll have noticed. Folk keep their voices down in the square these days, and nobody will say why. If you're going out, call on Mira, north of the square. She has a way with herbs, and with... other things. Old Man Hemlock at the General Store hears everything, and Borin at the forge keeps the tools sharp. You've a good heart, Elior. Don't let anyone talk you out of it.

speaker: narrator
text: Your grandmother, flour on her apron and her sleeves pushed up. She has raised you since your parents went away, and she keeps her hands busy when she would rather not answer.

speaker: narrator
text: You search the cottage thoroughly and discover a faded photograph hidden in a drawer.

speaker: narrator
text: You stop and think over what you know.

speaker: narrator
text: Shadows Over Willowbrook: Elior dreamed of a storm, a tune, and a figure in the dark that whispered his name. He woke with three words written down: …and let them rest…

speaker: narrator
text: Hint of Magic: You woke with three words written down and a tune still going in the house. Grandmother is at the hearth, and she will want to hear about the dream.

speaker: narrator
text: You rest for a moment, gathering your strength.

speaker: narrator
text: The flickering light reveals more of the room. A small loaf of bread and a journal appear in the light.

speaker: narrator
text: A small loaf of fresh, crusty bread. It smells delicious and could restore a bit of energy.

speaker: narrator
text: A leather-bound journal filled with Elior's careful handwriting. The pages are full of notes, sketches, and secrets.

speaker: narrator
text: This might come in handy, so you decide to pick it up.

speaker: narrator
text: Grandmother turns it over in her hands and gives it back.

speaker: grandmother
text: Keep it, love. My shelves are full enough.

speaker: narrator
text: You are not particularly hungry.

speaker: narrator
text: Grandmother has nothing to sell you.

speaker: grandmother
text: Back again? There's bread on the board, if you're hungry.

speaker: narrator
text: The ink is slightly smudged on this page, as if written in haste or with a trembling hand...

speaker: elior
text: The storm kept me up half the night. Then a light split the sky over the fields, and it was not lightning.

speaker: elior
text: When I slept, I dreamed. Dark, and rain on shutters I could not see. A man's hand lifted a child out of the dark. There was a tune, three notes up and home again, and a tall figure that whispered my name. When I answered it, it said three words more, and I wrote them down the moment I woke so I would not lose them: …and let them rest…

speaker: elior
text: I knew that voice. Not the way you know a neighbour's, but the way you know a song someone sang to you before you had words for it. It made my chest ache. I can't think from where.

speaker: elior
text: When I woke, the tune was still going. Someone out by the hearth was humming it.

speaker: narrator
text: When you go to her, she is humming at the hearth: a slow tune that climbs three notes and settles home again. You know it. You have known it all your life, and you could not say from where. She stops when she sees your face.

speaker: narrator
text: You tell her about the dream: the shadows, the figure, the voice calling your name, and how you were sure you had heard it before. She reaches for your hand and holds it tighter than she means to.

speaker: grandmother
text: That voice... did it say anything more? Anything but your name?

speaker: narrator
text: You tell her the three words you caught at the very end, the ones you wrote down before they could go: let them rest. She goes quiet. She turns to the bread on the board and does not turn back for a while.

speaker: grandmother
text: Some voices are older than memory.

speaker: narrator
text: She wipes her hands and looks at the journal under your arm.

speaker: grandmother
text: Your father wrote in one like that every night, at this table. Half of it I never understood. He thought the land was getting sick long before anyone else did. And there was one thing he kept coming back to: a way to call a thing back when it's nearly gone. Revive, he called it. He'd try it on my herbs when they wilted.

speaker: narrator
text: She almost smiles.

speaker: grandmother
text: Sometimes I think it worked.

speaker: narrator
text: As she speaks, the words your father wrote come back to you, and this time they stay.

speaker: narrator
text: You have learned revive.

speaker: narrator
text: Magic for real

speaker: narrator
text: You know a spell now, but when you reach for it the warmth comes and nothing answers. Grandmother says Mira has a way with herbs, and with other things.

speaker: narrator
text: Side quest complete

speaker: narrator
text: Grandmother told you of your father's journal, and his word for calling a thing back. It came to you as she spoke, and it stayed.

speaker: narrator
text: You already have it by heart: his words, and the way she told them.

speaker: narrator
text: Magic for real: You know a spell now, but when you reach for it the warmth comes and nothing answers. Grandmother says Mira has a way with herbs, and with other things.

speaker: narrator
text: The Faded Photograph

speaker: narrator
text: An old photograph of your parents, hidden away in a drawer. On the back is a line in your mother's hand.

speaker: narrator
text: An old, faded photograph. The image is barely visible, but you can make out two adults and a child. On the back, in your mother's handwriting, is a cryptic message:

speaker: narrator
text: Seek the truth where the river bends.

speaker: narrator
text: You search the cottage but find nothing new.

speaker: narrator
text: The Faded Photograph: An old photograph of your parents, hidden away in a drawer. On the back is a line in your mother's hand.

speaker: narrator
text: Your grandmother takes the photograph and holds it close to the window.

speaker: grandmother
text: The three of you. You'd not have been two. Your mother wouldn't stand still for it; that's why she's half a blur.

speaker: narrator
text: She hands it back, and turns to the bread.

speaker: narrator
text: Your grandmother turns the photograph over, and her thumb rests on the writing.

speaker: grandmother
text: That's her hand. She always wrote as if the ink were running out.

speaker: narrator
text: For a while she says nothing.

speaker: grandmother
text: Your parents didn't just leave, Elior. They went toward something. I begged them not to.

speaker: narrator
text: She hands the photograph back.

speaker: grandmother
text: Your mother loved the river. If anyone remembers what she did there, it's the old fisherman down at the Riverbank. Promise me you'll be careful.

speaker: narrator
text: Know your village

speaker: narrator
text: Something pulls at you to walk every lane of Willowbrook, and to look properly at the places you have passed a thousand times.

speaker: narrator
text: The Vegetable Field has withered under a grey sky: brittle leaves, cracked earth, and only a few stubborn carrots left.

speaker: narrator
text: Vegetable Field

speaker: narrator
text: Rows of withered crops stretch beneath a brooding gray sky. The earth is cracked and dry, with only a few stubborn carrots and a rusty hoe hinting at better days. A faint breeze rustles the brittle leaves, carrying the scent of soil and distant rain. These rows were green a month ago.

speaker: narrator
text: A shriveled, orange carrot barely clinging to life. It looks edible, but only just.

speaker: narrator
text: A gardening hoe with a rusted blade and a splintered handle. It might still be useful for tilling soil.

speaker: narrator
text: A small kitchen knife with a dull blade. It won't cut much, but could be sharpened.

speaker: narrator
text: You search around the Vegetable Field, but find nothing of interest beyond what you can already see.

speaker: narrator
text: Shadows Over Willowbrook: The Vegetable Field has withered under a grey sky: brittle leaves, cracked earth, and only a few stubborn carrots left.

speaker: narrator
text: Know your village: Something pulls at you to walk every lane of Willowbrook, and to look properly at the places you have passed a thousand times.

speaker: narrator
text: The ground is tough, and you unearth a small, tarnished coin! You quickly pocket it.

speaker: narrator
text: A small, circular piece of metal, likely used as currency. It has a simple stamp on one side.

speaker: narrator
text: The coin lands heads up. Seems like a regular coin, perhaps for trading.

speaker: narrator
text: You focus your will, a faint warmth spreads from your fingertips, and nothing answers it. The warmth is yours; the door it wants is not open yet.

speaker: narrator
text: Chicken Coop

speaker: narrator
text: A small wooden coop stands here, its planks patched and weathered. Nervous chickens cluck and flutter, their feathers ruffled as they dart between straw nests. The air is thick with the scent of hay and the occasional squawk. Sunbeams slip through the slats, casting striped shadows on the dirt floor. High on a rafter, out of reach, something glints where no hen could have put it.

speaker: narrator
text: A live, clucking chicken. It seems restless and might peck if you're not careful.

speaker: narrator
text: A freshly laid egg, still warm. It could be cooked or used in a recipe.

speaker: narrator
text: A soft white feather, likely from one of the chickens. It could be used for writing, crafting, or tickling.

speaker: narrator
text: You swing the rusty hoe, but it doesn't seem to have much effect here. It's a sturdy (but rusty) tool, though.

speaker: narrator
text: You search around the Chicken Coop, but find nothing of interest beyond what you can already see.

speaker: narrator
text: The chickens peck at the bread excitedly, and in the flapping commotion something shiny is knocked from a high rafter. It's a small key, hidden up there long ago by someone who did not want it found!

speaker: narrator
text: A small, rusty key. It looks like it might unlock something.

speaker: grandmother
text: So the chickens gave up my little secret. I tucked that key up in the coop rafters years ago. It opens the old shed by the mill. It was a workshop once... your father's. I never could bring myself to go in. It's dark as a cellar in there, dear; take the lantern with you.

speaker: narrator
text: Tilda looks it over with interest and gives it back.

speaker: tilda
text: Don't go giving your things away, love. People will talk.

speaker: narrator
text: Tilda has nothing to sell you.

speaker: tilda
text: The truth about what, love? You've lost me.

speaker: narrator
text: Village Square

speaker: narrator
text: The heart of Willowbrook: cobblestones around an old stone fountain, and a weathered notice board covered in faded announcements. Half the market stalls stand empty. The people at the others keep their voices down, and stop talking when you pass.

speaker: narrator
text: A sturdy wooden bucket with a rope handle. It's perfect for drawing water from a well or carrying supplies.

speaker: narrator
text: A faded piece of parchment pinned to the notice board. The writing is barely legible, but it might contain a clue or warning.

speaker: tilda
text: Have you seen the fields? Green on market day, grey by the next morning. My husband says it's the soil. He also said it would rain last Tuesday.

speaker: narrator
text: Tilda, the baker's wife, flour to the elbows. She knows what everyone in Willowbrook had for breakfast, and who they ate it with.

speaker: narrator
text: You search around the Village Square, but find nothing of interest beyond what you can already see.

speaker: narrator
text: The bucket is no use with that. Perhaps near something with water?

speaker: narrator
text: In the square, Tilda has more rumours than bread, and the people around her keep their voices down.

speaker: tilda
text: Last night, someone spotted a cloaked stranger near the old well, asking after an old amulet, from a family that left. Nobody would tell him a thing, and he took the road to the mill.

speaker: narrator
text: Shadows Over Willowbrook: In the square, Tilda has more rumours than bread, and the people around her keep their voices down.

speaker: narrator
text: The bucket is empty. The parched rows will need water from somewhere.

speaker: narrator
text: Village Well

speaker: narrator
text: An old stone well stands between the field and the forge, its stones worn smooth by countless hands. The water below lies dark and still, and a faint sour smell hangs in the cool, damp air. Moss creeps up the sides.

speaker: narrator
text: An old stone well, its surface worn smooth, its shaft disappearing into the depths. The water below is dark and still, and it smells sour, the way milk does when it has turned. Far down, something glints, or you think it does. It is much too deep to reach.

speaker: narrator
text: You search around the Village Well, but find nothing of interest beyond what you can already see.

speaker: narrator
text: The village well smells sour, and far down in the dark water something glints.

speaker: narrator
text: Shadows Over Willowbrook: The village well smells sour, and far down in the dark water something glints.

speaker: narrator
text: The bucket comes up from the well full of murky water.

speaker: narrator
text: A sturdy wooden bucket with a rope handle. It is full of murky water, with a sour smell drawn from the well.

speaker: narrator
text: The blacksmith gives it a glance and hands it back.

speaker: blacksmith
text: Can't melt it, can't mend it. No use to me, lad.

speaker: narrator
text: The blacksmith eyes the dull knife.

speaker: blacksmith
text: That edge has seen better days. I'll put it right for you, lad, but it'll cost a coin. Whetstones don't grow on trees.

speaker: narrator
text: The blacksmith eyes the coin.

speaker: blacksmith
text: A coin's no use to me without something to put an edge on, lad. Bring the dull knife as well.

speaker: narrator
text: Blacksmith's Forge

speaker: narrator
text: A hot, smoky forge. Coals glow in the hearth and the anvil rings. Hinges, ploughshares and horseshoes hang from the walls, waiting to be mended or fetched, and the blacksmith wipes his brow without putting down the hammer.

speaker: narrator
text: A heavy iron horseshoe, slightly bent. It might bring luck or be useful for repairs.

speaker: blacksmith
text: Mind the sparks, lad.

speaker: narrator
text: He doesn't stop hammering.

speaker: blacksmith
text: Borin. I make what this village breaks, and I mend what it won't throw away. Got anything with an edge gone soft? Bring it here.

speaker: narrator
text: Borin, the village smith: forearms like fence posts and an old burn on every knuckle. He talks while he works, and he doesn't stop working.

speaker: narrator
text: You search around the Blacksmith's Forge, but find nothing of interest beyond what you can already see.

speaker: blacksmith
text: Back again, lad? Forge is hot. What've you got for me?

speaker: narrator
text: The blacksmith pockets the coin and puts the dull knife to the whetstone. It sings for a minute. He tests the edge on his thumbnail before he hands it back.

speaker: narrator
text: You receive a sharp knife.

speaker: narrator
text: A well-sharpened knife. It looks like it could cut through almost anything.

speaker: blacksmith
text: How is that blade holding up? Keep that edge oiled, mind, or the damp will have it dull again before you know it.

speaker: narrator
text: Curiosity killed the cat

speaker: narrator
text: Old Man Hemlock has shut the General Store until his cat, Patches, comes home. She was last seen near the old well, where a locked shed keeps its secrets. What will you discover if you find a way inside?

speaker: narrator
text: Abandoned Shed

speaker: narrator
text: A rickety shed leans precariously at the edge of Willowbrook, its weathered boards creaking in the wind. Rusty tools and broken crates are scattered about a long workbench, and a thick layer of dust covers everything. Little light gets past the grimy boards, and the air smells of old earth and lamp oil.

speaker: narrator
text: It's a sturdy wooden door, locked tight. There's a keyhole visible.

speaker: narrator
text: The door is locked. Through a gap in the boards there is only dark, and a smell of dust.

speaker: narrator
text: Curiosity killed the cat: Old Man Hemlock has shut the General Store until his cat, Patches, comes home. She was last seen near the old well, where a locked shed keeps its secrets. What will you discover if you find a way inside?

speaker: narrator
text: The key turns in the lock! The shed door creaks open.

speaker: narrator
text: In the gloom you make out an old workbench and a few interesting things. From the shadows comes a frightened mew, and a small patchwork shape bolts behind the broken crates.

speaker: narrator
text: The mysterious box is locked, and there is no keyhole. The runes around the lid are the only way in, and they do not answer to hands.

speaker: narrator
text: A small nose twitches behind the crates. Curiosity gets the better of her.

speaker: narrator
text: A pair of green eyes blinks in the dark. With a small, uncertain mew, Patches creeps out, sniffs your fingers and lets you scoop her up. She is thin and dusty, but unhurt.

speaker: narrator
text: You carry Patches in your arms. Old Man Hemlock at the General Store will be glad to see her.

speaker: narrator
text: Patches was hiding in the Abandoned Shed. Carry her home to Old Man Hemlock at the General Store.

speaker: narrator
text: Patches sniffs at your offering from the shadows and stays put. Whatever it is, it isn't worth leaving the crates for. Her ears turn toward you, though, as if she's waiting to be called.

speaker: narrator
text: Patches flicks an ear at you, but the words mean nothing to her.

speaker: narrator
text: The shed door is unlocked and slightly ajar.

speaker: narrator
text: A small, ornate wooden box covered in strange runes. The lid is tightly shut, and it feels oddly heavy for its size. You sense something important is hidden inside.

speaker: narrator
text: A rusty, splintered shovel with a cracked wooden handle. It looks like it hasn't been used in years, but might still be useful for digging in soft earth.

speaker: narrator
text: A small cat with a patchwork coat of ginger, black and white, and wide green eyes.

speaker: narrator
text: Holding the lantern high, you rummage through the clutter of rusty tools and broken crates. Tucked away in dusty corners, you find a discarded fishing rod, and a small magnet!

speaker: narrator
text: A pair of frightened green eyes watches you from behind the crates.

speaker: narrator
text: Curiosity killed the cat: Patches was hiding in the Abandoned Shed. Carry her home to Old Man Hemlock at the General Store.

speaker: narrator
text: A simple fishing rod. It looks a bit flimsy.

speaker: narrator
text: A small, surprisingly strong magnet. It might be useful for retrieving metallic objects from hard-to-reach places.

speaker: narrator
text: You search around the shed again, but find nothing else of interest among the clutter.

speaker: narrator
text: You could force the magnet onto the rod, but it would likely prevent you from fishing — and you are really keen on doing some fishing!

speaker: narrator
text: The rod is too short to reach the water.

speaker: narrator
text: You lift the bucket, then think better of it. The sour water from the well would only sicken the soil further.

speaker: narrator
text: Patches sniffs the rug, circles twice and curls up at your grandmother's feet. She laughs softly.

speaker: grandmother
text: Well, that's settled, then. I'll send word to Hemlock this very afternoon. He's a kind old soul; he'll be glad she's safe, and his store will be open again by the time you get there.

speaker: narrator
text: You let Patches stay by your grandmother's hearth, and she sent word to Old Man Hemlock. The General Store is open again. Curiosity did not kill this cat after all.

speaker: narrator
text: Patches is asleep in the warm spot by the hearth. Your grandmother follows your gaze and smiles.

speaker: grandmother
text: She has the run of the cottage already. I'll not be lonely with that one about.

speaker: narrator
text: Patches blinks at you slowly from beside the hearth and begins to purr.

speaker: narrator
text: The shopkeeper hurries over the moment you come in.

speaker: shopkeeper
text: Your grandmother sent word, lad. Patches is safe and warm by her hearth. I'll not drag her back; she always did like a fire better than a draughty old store, and I can call in and see her.

speaker: shopkeeper
text: The reward was for bringing her home, and she found a new one. But you'll not leave empty-handed: take this rope, on the house, and there's always an apple to go with it. And the store's open again, so have a look around.

speaker: narrator
text: You receive a rope and an apple.

speaker: narrator
text: You search around the General Store, but find nothing of interest beyond what you can already see.

speaker: narrator
text: Patches peers out of your arms, and your grandmother reaches out to scratch her ears.

speaker: grandmother
text: Hemlock's Patches! Poor thing, she's all dust and bones.

speaker: narrator
text: She keeps scratching a while longer than she needs to.

speaker: grandmother
text: It's very quiet here, with you out all day. If you'd have her stay with me, say so, and I'll square it with Hemlock myself. Or carry her home to him. He'll be worried sick.

speaker: narrator
text: Mira gently but firmly stops you.

speaker: mira
text: Those herbs are part of my stores, Elior. They are not for taking, but for healing those who truly need them.

speaker: narrator
text: Mira puts her hand over the amulet before yours gets there.

speaker: mira
text: Not that one, Elior. Not yet. It has waited a long while for you; it can wait until you're ready.

speaker: narrator
text: Mira regards it, then shakes her head gently.

speaker: mira
text: I have no need for this, child.

speaker: narrator
text: Mira's Hut

speaker: narrator
text: A small hut hung with drying herbs: lavender, sage, and roots in bundles from the rafters. Shelves of bottles line the walls, every one labelled. Mira moves among them without looking, the way you move through your own kitchen.

speaker: narrator
text: A bundle of fragrant green herbs, known for their restorative properties. Useful for healing wounds or brewing potions.

speaker: narrator
text: A mysterious amulet inscribed with runes. At its centre, a sun rises over three linked rings. It is faintly warm, as if someone had only just set it down.

speaker: narrator
text: Mira looks up from the herbs she is tying.

speaker: mira
text: Elior. Come in, mind the sage.

speaker: narrator
text: She studies your face.

speaker: mira
text: You've been dreaming. It's written all over you. What brings you?

speaker: narrator
text: You tell Mira about the grey crops, the hushed square and the sour smell of the well. She stops tying herbs.

speaker: mira
text: None of that is weather.

speaker: narrator
text: She sets the bundle down.

speaker: mira
text: They say the king is ill, and no one can name it. The fields are ill, and no one can name that either. I think it's one wound, Elior, and we're feeling it in two places.

speaker: mira
text: There is a rare flower in the Hidden Glade. It only opens for someone the land trusts. Bring me one. If it opens for you, I'll know what I need to know.

speaker: mira
text: And look at that well again on your way. Water doesn't sour without a reason.

speaker: narrator
text: Mira, the village healer. Her hut smells of drying sage, and she looks at you a moment longer than people usually do.

speaker: narrator
text: You search around Mira's Hut, but find nothing of interest beyond what you can already see.

speaker: narrator
text: Mira says the sickness in the fields and the sickness of the king feel like one wound. She wants a rare flower from the Hidden Glade, one that opens only for someone the land trusts.

speaker: narrator
text: Shadows Over Willowbrook: Mira says the sickness in the fields and the sickness of the king feel like one wound. She wants a rare flower from the Hidden Glade, one that opens only for someone the land trusts.

speaker: narrator
text: The shopkeeper quickly steps over.

speaker: shopkeeper
text: Hold on there, friend! That sword is merchandise, not a free sample. If you want it, you'll need to buy it proper-like.

speaker: shopkeeper
text: Hold on there, friend! That armor is merchandise, not a free sample. If you want it, you'll need to buy it proper-like.

speaker: narrator
text: The shopkeeper chuckles and pushes it back across the counter.

speaker: shopkeeper
text: I sell things, lad. I don't take them in.

speaker: narrator
text: It feels perfectly balanced and ready for combat.

speaker: narrator
text: It looks like it would provide good protection if worn.

speaker: narrator
text: General Store

speaker: narrator
text: A cluttered shop with the shutters half down. Rope, apples, matches and trinkets crowd the shelves in the gloom. The shopkeeper stands at the window, watching the lane.

speaker: narrator
text: A long, sturdy coil of rope. Useful for climbing, tying, or hauling things.

speaker: narrator
text: A crisp, red apple. It looks fresh and delicious, perfect for a quick snack.

speaker: narrator
text: A small box of matches. Useful for lighting fires, candles, or lanterns.

speaker: narrator
text: A well-balanced iron sword with a sharp edge. The blade gleams with a faint sheen, and the leather-wrapped handle feels comfortable in your grip.

text: The warmth reaches the kit and it flinches from it. The wire is still in the leg; mending flesh around iron would be cruelty, and the kit knows it before you do.

text: The bush greens under your hand, every leaf at once. Life it has. It bears nothing; fruit wants something else of you.

speaker: narrator
text: The deer sniffs at it and turns its head away.

speaker: narrator
text: The deer has nothing to sell you.

speaker: narrator
text: A divine light surrounds deer, and they seem strengthened and more resolute.

speaker: narrator
text: A warm light settles over the deer. There was nothing in them that needed mending.

speaker: narrator
text: The cleansing runs over the deer and finds nothing to wash away.

speaker: narrator
text: Light fills the glade.

speaker: narrator
text: The darkness lifts, and sunlight comes down through the branches. The runes on the mossy stone stand out clear at last. They speak of a seed, a song, and the sun.

speaker: narrator
text: You read them slowly, and the spell comes with the reading. It does not wake in you the way the others did; this one you read, word by word, off the stone, and it feels like your own. You have learned the grow spell!

speaker: narrator
text: Carved beneath the runes, in a plainer hand, are words you can read:

speaker: narrator
text: Power follows purpose; purpose follows truth.

speaker: narrator
text: You read them aloud. They mean nothing to you, and yet they stay with you.

speaker: narrator
text: The grass at your feet stands a little taller. Nothing here was waiting for it.

speaker: narrator
text: The deer does not answer, not in words. It lifts its head toward the glowing stone, then dips it to you, slow and deliberate, as if in thanks.

speaker: narrator
text: It lifts its head toward the glowing stone, then dips it to you, slow and deliberate, as if in thanks.

speaker: narrator
text: The bush flourishes, and clusters of wild berries appear among its leaves!

speaker: narrator
text: A handful of small, juicy berries. They look edible, but you can't be sure they're safe.

speaker: grandmother
text: Look at you: wild berries, and your fingers purple to the knuckle, same as when you were six.

speaker: narrator
text: She tips them into a bowl.

speaker: grandmother
text: I'll make a pie. You'll be here to eat it, I hope.

speaker: narrator
text: Grandmother's eyes widen as she sees the locket.

speaker: grandmother
text: This... this was your mother's. It came to her from me, and to me from my mother, all the way back to the founders, so the old ones said. I thought she took it with her when she left.

speaker: narrator
text: She closes her hand around it for a moment. Then she goes to the chest at the foot of her bed and takes out something folded in paper.

speaker: grandmother
text: She left this with me the week before she went. 'When he's grown,' she said. I've never known when that was.

speaker: narrator
text: She looks at you.

speaker: grandmother
text: I suppose it's now.

speaker: narrator
text: You receive a travel cloak.

speaker: narrator
text: A heavy, hooded cloak made for travel. It offers warmth and protection from the elements.

speaker: narrator
text: Preparing for the road: Mira has tasked you with preparing for your journey. She says you will need: Magical protection

speaker: narrator
text: The priest shakes his head and folds your fingers back over it.

speaker: priest
text: Keep it, child. The road will want it more than I do.

speaker: narrator
text: The priest has nothing to sell you.

speaker: narrator
text: A divine light surrounds priest, and they seem strengthened and more resolute.

speaker: narrator
text: A warm light settles over the priest. There was nothing in them that needed mending.

speaker: narrator
text: The cleansing runs over the priest and finds nothing to wash away.

speaker: narrator
text: The priest smiles.

speaker: priest
text: The chapel is brighter for your kindness, child. The founders would be glad of you.

speaker: narrator
text: A quiet warmth settles on your shoulders and stays, the way the priest's hand did.

speaker: narrator
text: The priest studies you for a long moment, then smiles.

speaker: priest
text: The blessing sits well on you. The founders' light has not gone out of their line after all. Go gently on the road.

speaker: narrator
text: Preparing for the road: Mira has tasked you with preparing for your journey. She says you will need: Sturdy footwear

speaker: narrator
text: You have walked every corner of Willowbrook. The pull has gone quiet, and the village feels like home.

speaker: narrator
text: The merchant weighs it in his palm and hands it back.

speaker: merchant
text: I'd not get a copper for that in Greendale, friend.

speaker: merchant
text: That's kind, friend, but you'll want every bite of that where you're going. Keep it.

speaker: narrator
text: The merchant has nothing to sell you.

speaker: narrator
text: A divine light surrounds merchant, and they seem strengthened and more resolute.

speaker: narrator
text: A warm light settles over the merchant. There was nothing in them that needed mending.

speaker: narrator
text: The cleansing runs over the merchant and finds nothing to wash away.

speaker: narrator
text: Road to Greendale

speaker: narrator
text: The main road out of Willowbrook runs east under old oaks, their branches meeting overhead. The way is well trodden, lined with wildflowers and fallen leaves. A merchant's cart stands at the roadside, and his thin grey mare grazes beside it on three good shoes.

speaker: narrator
text: An old, rusty saw with a worn wooden handle. It looks like it could still cut through something soft, but might break on anything tough.

speaker: narrator
text: The map stays a plain map of Willowbrook. The hidden road will not show itself while something here is unfinished: the amulet Mira still keeps for you and your preparations for the road.

speaker: narrator
text: The merchant offers a friendly nod.

speaker: merchant
text: You'll want news, if you're bound for Greendale. It's a sombre city this season: they say King Alden has fallen ill, and no physician can name the sickness. And the roads have gone bad besides. I passed a cart on its side by the hill road, and nobody with it. And it's not only your fields that are failing. I've seen crops gone grey in every valley from here to the capital, ever since the king took to his bed. Keep to the daylight, friend. Boots, friend? I've one good pair of wandering boots left, walked in and soft, and the soles will outlast you. I'll not take coin for them; coin I can earn anywhere. Something small and fine would buy them. A ring, say. Failing that, my old mare threw a shoe on the hill road; a good iron horseshoe would do me nearly as well. Forgive me if I'm short, friend. I've not eaten since the hill road, and there's no inn this side of Greendale.

speaker: narrator
text: A travelling merchant with a loaded cart and a thin grey mare who stands on three good shoes. He has the look of a man two days from his last meal.

speaker: narrator
text: You search around the Road to Greendale, but find nothing of interest beyond what you can already see.

speaker: narrator
text: The merchant holds the shiny ring up to the light, and his eyebrows go up.

speaker: merchant
text: Now this is fine work. Older than it looks, too.

speaker: narrator
text: He looks at you, then away.

speaker: merchant
text: Well. A bargain's a bargain. The wandering boots are yours.

speaker: narrator
text: You receive a pair of wandering boots.

speaker: narrator
text: You have gathered all the items needed for your journey. With your preparations complete, you are ready to face whatever lies beyond Willowbrook.

speaker: narrator
text: Sturdy leather boots, well-worn and comfortable. They seem to hum with a faint energy, eager for the road.

speaker: narrator
text: The map stays a plain map of Willowbrook. The hidden road will not show itself while something here is unfinished: the amulet Mira still keeps for you.

speaker: narrator
text: The merchant grins.

speaker: merchant
text: You'll want news, if you're bound for Greendale. It's a sombre city this season: they say King Alden has fallen ill, and no physician can name the sickness. And the roads have gone bad besides. I passed a cart on its side by the hill road, and nobody with it. And it's not only your fields that are failing. I've seen crops gone grey in every valley from here to the capital, ever since the king took to his bed. Keep to the daylight, friend. How are the boots? Give them a week and they'll know your feet better than you do. Forgive me if I'm short, friend. I've not eaten since the hill road, and there's no inn this side of Greendale.

speaker: tilda
text: The water's clean! I've not had dough rise so light in a year. Was that you, Elior?

speaker: narrator
text: She looks at you, and waits.

speaker: narrator
text: You tell Tilda it was you: a spell, and a little help from the healer.

speaker: tilda
text: Magic? In Willowbrook? ... Well. I'll not tell a soul if you'd rather I didn't. But I'll know, and I'll be saving you the first loaf every morning.

speaker: tilda
text: I know, love. Your secret's safe with me, and so's your loaf.

speaker: narrator
text: The herb crowds its pot and spills green over the rim, twice what it was.

speaker: narrator
text: Mira raises an eyebrow.

speaker: mira
text: That was dear, that herb. Now there is more of it. I will not complain.

speaker: narrator
text: Mira looks you over: cloak, boots, pack. She nods once.

speaker: mira
text: You're ready. Or as ready as anyone gets.

speaker: narrator
text: She lifts the ancient amulet from its stand, puts it in your hand and closes your fingers over it. It is warm.

speaker: narrator
text: You now carry the ancient amulet.

speaker: narrator
text: Then, more quietly:

speaker: mira
text: I knew your parents better than I have said. Once you are truly ready, I will tell you.

speaker: narrator
text: She holds your hand a moment longer.

speaker: mira
text: A man came to my door at the turn of the month, in a grey cloak, asking after this. I told him I grow herbs.

speaker: mira
text: Your road leads to Greendale, Elior. Once there, show the amulet to no one lightly. Those who know what it is will find you.

speaker: narrator
text: Mira turns the rune token over in her fingers, and the color drains from her face.

speaker: mira
text: This is a fouling sigil, Elior. Dropped into a well, it sours the water from below, slowly, so that no one thinks to look.

speaker: mira
text: The well did not sicken. Someone poisoned it on purpose.

speaker: narrator
text: You tell her of the black-iron mechanism at the mill, and the twisted rune on its housing. She nods slowly.

speaker: mira
text: The same hand, then. The mill stands on old power, and that thing was drinking it. You did well to stop it.

speaker: mira
text: The cloaked stranger the villagers whisper about.

speaker: narrator
text: She stops, as if she has said more than she meant to.

speaker: mira
text: Whoever carried this was not here to spoil a well and leave. They were searching Willowbrook for something.

speaker: narrator
text: She is quiet a moment.

speaker: mira
text: Or for someone.

speaker: narrator
text: She presses the token back into your palm.

speaker: mira
text: Keep it close, and keep it hidden.

speaker: narrator
text: Mira named the token a fouling sigil: someone poisoned the well on purpose. Whoever carried it, perhaps the cloaked stranger the villagers whisper about, was searching Willowbrook for something, or for someone.

speaker: narrator
text: Mira closes your fingers over the rune token without taking it.

speaker: mira
text: I have told you what I know of it. Keep it hidden, and keep your eyes open.

speaker: narrator
text: Shadows Over Willowbrook: Mira named the token a fouling sigil: someone poisoned the well on purpose. Whoever carried it, perhaps the cloaked stranger the villagers whisper about, was searching Willowbrook for something, or for someone.

speaker: narrator
text: A mysterious amulet inscribed with runes. At its centre, a sun rises over three linked rings. It is faintly warm in your hand.

speaker: narrator
text: Mira doesn't look up from her herbs.

speaker: mira
text: Still here? Go and say a proper goodbye to your grandmother. Then go.

speaker: tilda
text: Mira's amulet... you're leaving, aren't you? Well. Don't you dare go without a proper send-off from the bakery. And mind you come home, love.

speaker: narrator
text: Her eyes fall on the amulet you carry, and she goes very still.

speaker: grandmother
text: So it's true, then.

speaker: narrator
text: She turns the loaf on the board, though it does not need turning.

speaker: grandmother
text: Come back to me, child.

speaker: narrator
text: A mysterious amulet inscribed with runes. At its centre, a sun rises over three linked rings. It hums softly in your hand, as if answering something stirring beneath the floor.

speaker: narrator
text: A mysterious amulet inscribed with runes. At its centre, a sun rises over three linked rings. It glows in your hand, brightest when you hold it near the mossy stone.

speaker: narrator
text: Footsteps hurry along the road behind you.

speaker: narrator
text: Your grandmother has walked all the way out from the village. She tugs the travel cloak straight on your shoulders.

speaker: grandmother
text: Wear your mother's cloak. She'd want you warm.

speaker: grandmother
text: The merchant showed me the ring he had of you. It was your mother's wedding ring, child. No, don't fret; she'd have given it for your boots in a heartbeat.

speaker: grandmother
text: Old Hemlock is telling the whole square how you found his Patches.

speaker: narrator
text: Her hand finds the amulet at your chest and closes around it.

speaker: grandmother
text: This was theirs, you know. Aren and Lysa's.

speaker: narrator
text: In all your years, you have never once heard her say their names.

speaker: grandmother
text: They gave it to Mira to keep for you, until you were ready. And someone has come to Willowbrook looking for it. Keep it hidden, child.

speaker: narrator
text: She kisses your brow, and turns for home before you can see her cry.

speaker: narrator
text: As you look back at Willowbrook, the chapel bell rings once, though no hand is on the rope.

speaker: narrator
text: The map aligns with the landscape, revealing a hidden path that shortens the journey to Greendale. You tuck your parents' amulet beneath your mother's cloak, and set forth.

speaker: narrator
text: Main quest complete

speaker: narrator
text: The well was poisoned on purpose, and whoever did it came to Willowbrook looking for an amulet. Elior carries that amulet now, on the road to Greendale.

speaker: narrator
text: Act I complete. The Call to Adventure.

speaker: narrator
text: The amulet was your parents'. And someone has come to Willowbrook looking for it.
